findings.text: §23's Why says `_held_worktree_records` is "recomputed on every tick for every session", but it is already memoised by exactly the key §23's Deliverable prescribes: `obligations.py:2199-2208` builds `key = (project, repository, _held_records_signature(...))` and serves the result through `file_memo.memoized_key`, with `_held_records_signature` (`obligations.py:2221-2250`) covering the ledger file stamp, git's worktree registry and the `(run_id, worktree)` set of live pointers; that memo is in the profiled tree (`git cat-file -p b3fb5d5693:reckon/crew/obligations.py` shows `memoized_key` at the same function) and landed in `258296b3c9 perf(crew): memoise the obligations a steady tick rebuilds` on 7 November, before the profile was taken; measured at this revision, two back-to-back calls read for 17.65 s then 0.16 s with the read function entered once, so the work is not "recomputed on every tick" and §23 as written would change nothing; the profile samples (93 of the station's 243 samples, 23% of the file's 397) sit inside `_held_worktree_records_read` — `_run_namings > ledger.runs > read_records` in 15 of the 24 matching stacks — which is a cache MISS path, so the real lever is what moves `_held_records_signature` between ticks (the live-pointer set and the ledger stamp) and the whole-ledger walk each miss performs, not the absence of a key; "for every session" is also wrong, since `obligation_snapshot.py:1326` calls it once per project per tick

findings.reason: the deliverable points the worker at a cache that exists and at a key change that increases rebuilds, so the node would ship no cost reduction and could not be reviewed against the section's premise.
